docs.text: HardFOC CI and documentation platform General CI Tools ¶ Reusable GitHub Actions workflows that every HardFOC repository calls: C/C++ lint and analysis, host builds and tests, the documentation platform, link and lint checks, releases, and one required CI gate. Callers pin @v1 and get fixes without breaking changes. Quickstart Workflow catalogue Source on GitHub A repository keeps a few short caller workflows; the jobs, the pinned tools and the checks live here. Every third-party action is pinned to a commit SHA, so @v1 pins everything a caller runs. What you get ¶ One required check. ru-ci-gate turns every job of a workflow into CI gate / gate . C++ checks that agree with the compiler. ru-host-ci builds, runs ctest, then clang-tidy 18 and cppcheck over the same compile database. The documentation platform. ru-mkdocs-publish builds a site with the shared theme in packages/hardfoc-mkdocs-theme , checks it, audits it and publishes it, versioned or not ( platform guide ). Releases without breaking callers. Semver tags, a moving v1 , an automatic patch release on every merge, and a check that stops a breaking change from landing without a major ( Versioning ). A permissions contract. Each workflow asks for the least it needs, per job, and the self-CI holds it to the documented table . Documentation style guide ¶ What every HardFOC documentation site contains, how its pages are written and what a README looks like. The pilot site, hardfoc/hf-tmc9660-driver , follows every rule here; copy its structure. Voice ¶ Plain and specific. "SPI mode 3, up to 10 MHz", not "supports high-speed SPI". Numbers, names, units. Second person, present tense, active voice. "Call init() before anything else", not "The init function should be called". Short sentences. One idea each. A paragraph is three to five sentences. No hype, no filler. No "simply", "just", "easily", "powerful", "comprehensive", "seamless", "robust". No emoji in headings, lists or tables. No walls of bold. No exclamation marks. Sentence case for titles and headings: "Bus settings", not "Bus Settings". British or American spelling : either, consistently within a repository. True statements only. Every API name, signature, pin, register and number is checked against the headers or the datasheet. When something is derived rather than measured, say so. Never mention how the page was produced. No "generated by", no tool or assistant names. Every page ¶ A title ( # Title , level one, exactly one), matching its navigation entry. A purpose line right under it: one sentence saying what the reader gets from the page. The theme renders it as the lead paragraph. Sections ( ## ) in the order a reader needs them. A section that is only a link list belongs in a table or in the navigation instead. A next step when there is an obvious one ( Next: [Porting](porting.md) ). No Jekyll front matter, no Liquid. Material front matter is allowed only for hide: (the home page hides the navigation and table of contents). Components ¶ The theme styles these; use them instead of inventing markup. Need Write Notes A warning that prevents damage or lost hours !!! warning "Title" / !!! danger At most two per page. note , tip , example for the rest Optional detail ??? note "Title" Collapsed by default Alternatives (SPI / UART, ESP-IDF / CMake) === "SPI" tabs Same structure in each tab Code fenced block with a language; title="file.cpp" for a file Code from a compiled file: --8<-- "tests/docs/x.cpp:section" Registers, parameters, pins, options a table Header row, units in the header, code font for names Bit fields a table inside
Offset and name columns get code font Sequence or state machine a mermaid fence Themed for light and dark automatically Architecture, signal flow, layouts a figkit figure Light and dark from one layout, checked for contrast A light-only image (vendor SVG, photo) ![alt](x.svg){ .hf-plate } Sits on a white plate in dark mode Steps

Home page; four to six cards Chip card ¶
Smart gate driver with on-chip FOC TMC9660 Analog Devices (Trinamic)
Interface : SPI mode 3 up to 10 MHz, or UART Supply : 7.7 V to 70 V [ Datasheet ]( datasheet/tmc9660.pdf ) · [ Reference manual ]( datasheet/ref.pdf )
Five to seven rows: function, interface (mode, speed, address), supply, key limits, package, and the mode the driver uses. A board uses class="hf-chip hf-chip--board" with MCU, power input, connectors, chips on board. Code ¶ It compiles against the real API. In a C++ repository, every snippet longer than one line lives in build (an OBJECT library, warnings on) and is included in the page with --8<-- "tests/docs/x.cpp:name" . Instantiate the driver template over the documented port so the whole API is compiled. It is the smallest complete thing. Includes, the object, the calls, the error check. No // ... in a block that claims to be complete. It checks results. Every driver call returns a status: show what to do with it. Names are real. A reader can paste them. One-line inline names ( setTargetVelocityRpm() ) are checked by searching the headers. The README quickstart is a generated region ( ) copied from the same compiled file, so it cannot drift. Figures ¶ figkit for architecture and anything drawn from the code: one module per figure in docs/diagrams/figures/.py , data() reads the facts from the headers, build() lays out cards. The build refuses text under 4.5:1 contrast in either theme, overlaps and missing alt text; hardfoc-docs figures --check fails CI when the code changed and the figure did not. Embed with / . Mermaid for sequences and state machines. Vendor diagrams only as SVG or compressed PNG, with { .hf-plate } , never screenshots of PDFs. Alt text on every image: one sentence that says what the figure shows, not "diagram". The build fails on a missing alt. PDFs (datasheets, manuals) live in docs/datasheet/ and are linked, never embedded; the site links them on GitHub, which renders them. Tables ¶ Use a table whenever there are three or more items with the same attributes: pins, registers, parameters, options, commands, error codes, compile-time switches. Put units in the header ( Range (V) ), names in code font, and keep cells short; long prose goes under the table. Link repository files relatively ( [`inc/x.hpp`](../inc/x.hpp) ); the plugin turns them into GitHub links at the commit that was built. Link the API reference with api/...html ; the link check verifies it after Doxygen is merged. External links go to the primary source (vendor page, datasheet, specification). configuration references under Guides . Navigation ( docs/.nav.yml ) is always five tabs: nav : - Home : index.md - Get started : [ Quickstart , Installation , Hardware ] - Concepts : [ Architecture , deep dives ... ] - Guides : [ API guide , Configuration , Porting , Examples , Troubleshooting ] - Reference : [ API reference , Testing and CI , Figures , Changelog ] Core library ( hf-core* , hf-utils-* , hf-*-interface-wrap , hf-pincfg ) ¶ Home (hero, what problem it solves, a feature list, a "used by" table), Quickstart (smallest use), Concepts (the model the library implements, with a figure), API guide (by task), API reference, Integration (CMake / ESP-IDF, configuration macros), Testing and CI, Changelog. HAL ( hf-hal-* ) ¶ Home with a board card ( hf-chip hf-chip--board ): MCU, power, connectors, chips on board; Quickstart (flash an example, see output); Hardware (block diagram figure, pin map as a generated table from the pin configuration, connectors, power tree); Architecture (managers, how drivers are wired, figure); one guide page per board function; API reference; Examples; Bring-up and troubleshooting; Changelog. Decisions as ADRs under Reference. CI and tool repositories ( hf-general-ci-tools , hf-espidf-ci-tools , hf-espidf-project-tools ) ¶ Home (what it provides, a table of workflows or scripts), Quickstart (the smallest caller), one page per workflow or script (purpose, jobs and permissions, inputs table generated from the YAML, example caller, failure modes), Versioning, Migration guides, Changelog. README standard ¶ The README is the front door on GitHub. It is short and points to the site. # Name and a hero line : one sentence, what it is and what it does. Badges that are true , in this order, only those that exist: CI (the main test workflow, branch=main ), docs (the docs workflow, linking the site), license, latest release (only once a release exists). No coverage badge without coverage, no "PRs welcome", no badge for a language version. The documentation link in bold. One diagram : the layer or block figure (figkit marker). A 30-second example : the generated quickstart region. What it does : five to seven bullets. Install : the submodule line and the CMake lines. Documentation : a table of the five or six most useful pages, linked to the site ( /latest/... ). Tests : one command line. License : one line. No table of contents, no walls of emoji, no feature lists with check marks, no badges that link nowhere, no duplicated API tables (that is the site's job). docs.text: Migrating a repository to MkDocs ¶ Move one repository's documentation from the Jekyll (just-the-docs) site to the HardFOC MkDocs platform, from a clean checkout to a published, versioned site. Plan on half a day for a driver: the mechanical part takes minutes, the rest is rewriting pages to the style guide . The pilot is hardfoc/hf-tmc9660-driver : when a step is unclear, look at what that repository does. docs.text: Versioning and releases ¶ Many repositories call these reusable workflows. When all of them used @main , one bad commit here broke every one of them at once. Versioning exists so that does not happen again. Scheme ¶ Release tags are immutable semver tags: v1.0.0 , v1.1.0 , v1.1.1 , and so on. The moving major tag ( v1 ) always points at the newest v1.x.y release. Callers pin the major tag : uses : hardfoc/hf-general-ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-cpp-lint.yml@v1 They receive fixes and new optional inputs automatically, never a breaking change. A caller that needs to be fully reproducible can pin an exact tag ( @v1.2.0 ) or a commit SHA. - @main is the development line. Its first users are the self-tests in this repository. What is breaking ¶ Anything that can make an existing, correct caller fail: Change Why it breaks A reusable workflow removed or renamed uses: no longer resolves An input removed Callers that pass it get startup_failure An input's type changed Callers that pass the old type get startup_failure An input or secret made required, or a new required one added Callers that do not pass it get startup_failure An output removed Callers that read it get empty values A job needs a permission it did not need before Callers that grant the old set get startup_failure A breaking change needs a major bump ( v1 → v2 ). It is listed under ### Breaking in the Unreleased section of CHANGELOG.md . On pull requests, the self-CI ( .github/scripts/check_contract.py ) compares each ru-*.yml with the base branch. It fails if it finds one of these changes and that heading is missing. Everything else is a minor release (new workflow, new optional input, new output) or a patch release (bug fix, action bump, documentation). Deprecating instead of removing ¶ To retire an input within a major: Keep declaring it, so callers that pass it keep starting. Prefix its description with Deprecated: and say what replaces it. Ignore it, or map it onto the replacement. When it is set, emit a ::warning:: that names the replacement. List it under ### Deprecated in the changelog. Remove it in the next major, and list the removal under ### Breaking . Automatic patch releases ¶ Every push to main is released: release.yml tags the commit vX.Y.(Z+1) after the highest release, creates the GitHub Release and moves vX . Callers pinned to @v1 therefore get each merged fix without anyone cutting a release. Nothing is tagged when the commit is already released, or when CHANGELOG.md 's Unreleased section has a ### Breaking heading: the self-CI contract check forces that heading on any breaking change, and a breaking change needs a new major, cut by hand as below. Minor releases (new features worth a line in the notes) are also cut by hand. Cutting a release (maintainers) ¶ Move the Unreleased entries in CHANGELOG.md under a new ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD heading, and merge that to main . Tag the merge commit and push the tag: git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "v1.0.0" git push origin v1.0.0 release.yml then creates the GitHub Release with generated notes. If the tag is the highest v1.*.* release, it also force-updates v1 to the same commit. A pre-release tag ( v1.1.0-rc.1 ) gets a pre-release and leaves v1 alone. A patch to an older minor does not move v1 backwards. The release workflow pushes v1 with the workflow token. If a tag ruleset protects v* , allow GitHub Actions to update it, or move the tag by hand. Re-runs use the old revision ¶ Re-run failed jobs reruns the workflow at the revision the original run resolved, including the revision of each reusable workflow. After a fix lands here, or after v1 moves, start a new run instead: push a commit, use Run workflow , or close and reopen the pull request. Keeping callers current ¶ Callers pinned to @v1 need nothing more for minor and patch releases. For majors, and for callers that pin exact tags or SHAs, Dependabot with package-ecosystem: github-actions proposes the update, because it also tracks uses: references to reusable workflows. Inside this repository ¶ The workflows in this repository pin third-party actions to full commit SHAs with a # vX.Y.Z comment. Dependabot ( .github/dependabot.yml ) keeps both current.

docs.text: Changelog ¶ Every change to the reusable workflows, the theme package and the tools, newest first, from CHANGELOG.md . [Unreleased] ¶ Added (unversioned sites, link check) ¶ ru-mkdocs-publish.yml : versioning input (default true ). false builds an unversioned site (the organisation portal) and publishes it from the default branch as the whole content of the deployment branch, at its root, in one ordinary commit; tags publish nothing. The custom domain comes from a CNAME file in the site ( docs/CNAME ), never from what the branch held before, so a stale CNAME cannot take the site over. Theme plugin: versioned option (unset: versioned, except <org>.github.io ), overridden by HARDFOC_DOCS_VERSIONED ; an unversioned site gets the Pages root as site_url and no version selector. hardfoc-docs publish-root : the publish step for unversioned sites, with unit tests against a scratch remote. ru-docs-linkcheck.yml : exclude_own_site (default true ) skips links to the repository's own Pages site on pull requests and until its latest/ answers, so a repository's first MkDocs pull request no longer fails on its own /latest/ links. ru-mkdocs-publish.yml : check_commands run with GH_TOKEN set to the job's read-only token, so a site can generate pages from the GitHub API at build time (the organisation portal's repository catalogue). Theme: a filterable catalogue component ( .hf-filter search field, .hf-chipbtn topic buttons, .hf-repo cards), used by the organisation portal's repository list. Theme: navigation.prune is on by default, so a page carries only the navigation it shows; on a site of about 85 pages it halves the HTML of every page and keeps it inside the Lighthouse performance budget. Theme package unit tests ( packages/hardfoc-mkdocs-theme/tests/ ), run by the self-CI. docs.text: Permissions contract ¶ What each reusable workflow needs from its caller, and the rules that keep that list true. Why it matters ¶ A called workflow cannot have more permissions than its caller grants. When a job of a reusable workflow asks for more, GitHub refuses the whole run before any job starts ( startup_failure ), in every repository that calls it. So a workflow here asks for the least it needs, per job, and the README and this page say exactly what that is. What each workflow needs ¶ Grant at least the "Caller grants" column on the calling job, or at the top of the calling workflow. The table is read from the workflow files. Workflow Caller grants Job: permissions ru-ci-gate.yml contents: read gate : contents: read ru-cpp-analysis.yml contents: read cppcheck : contents: read ru-cpp-lint.yml contents: read , pull-requests: write lint : contents: read , pull-requests: write ru-docs-linkcheck.yml contents: read link-check : contents: read ru-docs-publish.yml contents: write input-validation : none quality-checks : contents: read version-detection : contents: read build : contents: write ru-host-ci.yml contents: read host : contents: read ru-markdown-lint.yml contents: read markdownlint : contents: read ru-mkdocs-publish.yml contents: write build : contents: read quality : contents: read deploy : contents: write ru-release.yml contents: write release : contents: write ru-yaml-lint.yml contents: read yamllint : contents: read The rules ¶ The self-CI ( check_permissions.py in the workflow contract checks job) fails a pull request when: Rule Why A reusable workflow sets top-level permissions: Permissions are per job, so a read-only job never holds a write token A job of a reusable workflow has no permissions: mapping It would inherit everything the caller granted A workflow's job permissions differ from its row in the README table More breaks callers; less means the table asks for too much A reusable workflow has no row, or a row names no workflow The table is the contract callers read A caller in this repository grants less than the contract The self-tests would hit startup_failure A new permission on an existing workflow is a breaking change: it needs a ### Breaking entry in the changelog and a new major ( Versioning ). The "no bare && tail" rule ¶ GitHub runs run: blocks with bash -e , and a script's exit status is that of its last command. A last line such as [ -n "$X" ] && echo "..." fails the step whenever the condition is false, although -e ignores the same line anywhere else. check_run_tails.py fails any run: block that ends that way; write an if ... fi instead. Next: the workflow catalogue .

docs.text: GitHub runs run: blocks with bash -e , and a script's exit status is that of its last command. A last line such as [ -n "$X" ] && echo "..." fails the step whenever the condition is false, although -e ignores the same line anywhere else. check_run_tails.py fails any run: block that ends that way; write an if ... fi instead. docs.text: ru-ci-gate ¶ One required status check per repository: it passes only when every other CI job passed. ru-ci-gate.yml turns the results of all jobs in a workflow into a single check. A repository's ruleset then requires that one check instead of a list of job names that has to be updated whenever jobs are added, renamed or split. Caller pattern ¶ Add the gate as the last job of the CI workflow: jobs : build : # ... lint : # ... docs : # ... ci-gate : name : CI gate needs : [ build , lint , docs ] # every other job in this workflow if : always() # required, see below uses : hardfoc/hf-general-ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-ci-gate.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : needs_json : ${{ toJSON(needs) }} allow_skipped : docs # optional: jobs that may be skipped Then, in the repository ruleset (or branch protection), require only the status check named: CI gate / gate GitHub names checks from a called workflow <calling job name> / <called job name> , so with name: CI gate on the calling job the check is always CI gate / gate , in every repository. Rules ¶ The gate passes if and only if every job in needs finished with success , or with skipped and is listed in allow_skipped . failure , cancelled , and an unlisted skipped all fail it. if: always() is required. Without it, a failing job causes the gate to be skipped, and a skipped required check counts as passing . Every job must be in needs . A job outside needs can fail without failing the gate. With verify_needs: true (the default) the gate reads the calling workflow file and fails if either rule above is broken. It also fails if allow_skipped names a job that is not in needs , which catches typos. Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description needs_json string required The caller's needs context as JSON: the expression toJSON(needs) allow_skipped string empty Jobs (ids from needs ) that may be skipped without failing the gate, separated by commas, spaces or newlines. Every other job must succeed. verify_needs boolean true Read the calling workflow file and fail if a job is missing from the gate's needs , or if the gate job lacks if: always() . Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Permissions Steps gate (gate) contents: read Evaluate needed jobs contents: read is used to read the calling workflow file. Jobs that run conditionally ¶ A job that is skipped by design, for example a deploy job that runs only on main , goes in allow_skipped . A job that is skipped because something it needs failed is reported as skipped too. That case is still caught: the failed upstream job is itself in needs , so the gate fails on it.

docs.text: ru-cpp-analysis ¶ Run cppcheck over source folders, without a build, and keep the report as an artifact. ru-cpp-analysis.yml runs cppcheck in a container ( ghcr.io/facthunder/cppcheck ) over paths . It needs no compile database, so it suits header-only drivers and repositories without a host build; with a CMake build, ru-host-ci runs cppcheck on the compiler's own database instead. What it does ¶ Checks out the repository. Runs cppcheck with --enable=<enable> , --std=<std> , inline suppressions, -i for each exclude path, and --force / --max-configs when set. missingIncludeSystem and unmatchedSuppression are suppressed, because system headers are not mounted. Uploads cppcheck_report.xml and the console output as the cppcheck-report artifact (14 days). With strict: true , fails the job when the report is not empty. docs.text: ru-cpp-lint ¶ Check C and C++ formatting with clang-format and lint with clang-tidy, with results as annotations on the pull request. ru-cpp-lint.yml runs cpp-linter-action with the repository's own .clang-format and .clang-tidy . It needs no build: clang-tidy runs without a compile database, so it sees headers and defines only as far as it can guess them. A repository with a CMake host build gets more exact results from ru-host-ci . What it does ¶ Checks out the repository. Links clang_format_config and clang_tidy_config to .clang-format and .clang-tidy at the root when they live elsewhere (the HardFOC layout keeps them in _config/ ). A missing file is a warning, not an error. Lists the files it will lint ( git ls-files with extensions , without ignore ), so the log shows the scope. Runs clang-format ( style: file ) and clang-tidy at clang_version , on every file or only on changed files and lines, with annotations, a step summary and, optionally, one thread comment on the pull request. docs.text: ru-docs-linkcheck ¶ Check every link in a repository's Markdown, external ones included, with lychee. ru-docs-linkcheck.yml runs lychee over Markdown files in the repository. It complements ru-mkdocs-publish , whose link check runs offline on the built site: this one also follows external links, and checks Markdown that is not part of a site (READMEs, examples). What it does ¶ Checks out the repository, with submodules when checkout_recursive is set. Works out the repository's own Pages site ( https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/ ) and leaves links to it out of the check on pull requests, where the pages a change links to are not published yet, and on other events while its latest/ (the root, for <owner>.github.io ) does not answer, as before a repository's first MkDocs publish. Turn this off with exclude_own_site: false . Runs lychee over paths with the timeout, retries and exclusions set by the inputs, and a lychee.toml when config_file names one. Being replaced New sites use ru-mkdocs-publish . Repositories still on this workflow move with Migrating to MkDocs . This workflow keeps working for them under @v1 . docs.text: ru-host-ci ¶ Build, test and analyse a CMake project on the host, with clang-tidy 18 and cppcheck over the compiler's own compile database. ru-host-ci.yml runs the native (host) half of a C/C++ project's CI in one job: Configure. Uses cmake --preset <preset> when preset is set, otherwise cmake -S <source_dir> -B <build_dir> -G Ninja . Either way it passes -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON . Build. Runs cmake --build <build_dir> --parallel . Test. Runs ctest --test-dir <build_dir> --output-on-failure . Select files. Picks translation units from compile_commands.json . A unit is analysed if its path relative to the repository root matches tidy_paths . Units that match exclude_paths and anything generated in the build tree are dropped. The selection is written as a filtered database, so both analysers see exactly the same files. Analyse. Runs clang-tidy 18 ( -p <build_dir> ) and cppcheck ( --project=<filtered database> ) on that set. Both see the include paths and defines the compiler sees, so no configuration is guessed. Report. Findings appear as annotations. The reports, the file list and the database are uploaded as an artifact. With fail_on_findings: true (the default), any finding fails the job. clang-tidy exits 0 even when it prints warnings, so the workflow counts file:line:col: warning|error: ... [check] lines itself. It ignores compiler warnings echoed as clang-diagnostic-* , except clang-diagnostic-error . cppcheck findings are lines of severity error, warning, performance, portability or style; information lines (analysis limits) do not count. Minimal caller ¶ jobs : host : uses : hardfoc/hf-general-ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-host-ci.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : preset : host-debug build_dir : build/host-debug # the preset's binaryDir, from the repo root tidy_paths : "^(src|include|apps)/" cppcheck_suppressions : tools/lint/cppcheck-suppressions.txt Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description preset string empty CMake configure preset (from CMakePresets.json in source_dir). Empty: configure with -S source_dir -B build_dir. source_dir string . CMake source directory, relative to the repository root build_dir string build/host Build directory, relative to the repository root. With a preset this must be the preset's binaryDir; compile_commands.json is read from here. cmake_args string empty Extra arguments for the configure step (space separated) build_type string Debug CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE when no preset is used run_tests boolean true Run ctest after the build ctest_args string empty Extra arguments for ctest (space separated) tidy_paths string empty Python regular expression matched (re.search) against each translation unit's path relative to the repository root. Only matching files are given to clang-tidy and cppcheck. Empty: every file in the database. exclude_paths string (^|/)(third_party|external|vendor|_deps)/ Python regular expression; translation units whose relative path matches are never analysed, and findings in matching files are not counted. The build directory is always excluded. run_clang_tidy boolean true Run clang-tidy 18 on the selected files clang_tidy_config string empty Path to a .clang-tidy file. Empty: clang-tidy's normal lookup from each source file run_cppcheck boolean true Run cppcheck on the selected files cppcheck_suppressions string empty Path to a cppcheck --suppressions-list file (optional) cppcheck_enable string warning,performance,portability cppcheck --enable value fail_on_findings boolean true Fail the job when clang-tidy or cppcheck report findings apt_packages string empty Extra apt packages to install before configuring (space separated) submodules string false actions/checkout submodules value: false, true or recursive runs_on string ubuntu-24.04 Runner label (Ubuntu 24.04 or newer, for clang-tidy-18 from apt) artifact_name string host-ci-reports Name of the uploaded report artifact Outputs: tidy_findings and cppcheck_findings , the counts of findings (empty when a tool did not run). docs.text: ru-mkdocs-publish ¶ Build, check, audit and publish a HardFOC documentation site with the shared theme, versioned or not. ru-mkdocs-publish.yml builds a HardFOC documentation site with the shared theme, checks it, audits it and publishes it to gh-pages as a versioned site with mike , with the Doxygen API reference under api/ . Migrating to MkDocs moves a repository onto it; the style guide says what its pages contain. Where the theme comes from ¶ The theme, the plugin, figkit and the pinned toolchain are the hardfoc-mkdocs-theme package in packages/hardfoc-mkdocs-theme . Every job installs it with pip from the commit this workflow runs from (the job context's workflow_repository and workflow_sha ), so a caller pinned to @v1 builds with the theme released in v1 , and a branch under review builds with that branch's theme. theme_ref overrides the ref. A repository's own requirements-docs.txt , if it has one, is installed afterwards for extra plugins. What runs when ¶ Event Build + checks Lighthouse + screenshots Publish Pull request Yes Yes Never, whatever deploy says Push to the default branch Yes Yes Version dev (when deploy is true); dev also holds latest until the first release Push of a vX.Y.Z tag Yes Yes Version vX.Y.Z ( release_version: minor : X.Y ), and latest moves to it With versioning: false (the organisation portal) there are no versions: see Unversioned sites . The site root redirects to latest . Aliases are symlinks, so the API reference added to a version folder is reachable through them too. Material's version selector in the header lists every version. Jobs and permissions ¶ The caller grants contents: write , even one that never publishes (pull requests, deploy: false ): GitHub checks the permissions of every job of a called workflow before the run starts, whatever the job's if . Job Permissions Steps build contents: read Check out (plus submodule_paths ), install the theme, run check_commands ( hardfoc-docs check ), mkdocs build --strict , Doxygen into api/ (with the HardFOC API stylesheet when the Doxyfile has none), lychee --offline --include-fragments on the merged site, upload docs-site quality contents: read Lighthouse CI (median of 3 runs, mobile emulation) on the home page and the first navigation pages against lighthouse_budgets , upload lighthouse-report ; Playwright screenshots at 375 and 1280 px, light and dark, upload docs-screenshots deploy contents: write Versioned: prune the pre-MkDocs site from gh-pages ( prune_legacy ), mike deploy , add the API reference to the version folder, mike set-default latest , root 404.html , push (never force). Unversioned: hardfoc-docs publish-root commits the built site as the whole branch, push (never force) Every action is pinned to a commit SHA with its version in a comment. The first publish ¶ A repository with an older (Jekyll / Doxygen) site on gh-pages : everything at the top of the branch that is not a mike version or alias is removed in one commit before mike writes (kept: versions.json , index.html once mike owns it, 404.html , .nojekyll , CNAME , robots.txt ). A repository without gh-pages : mike creates the branch. In both cases the root gets mike's redirect to latest/ and a 404.html that sends old addresses to the same page under latest/ ( /docs/x/ , /development/x/ to latest/x/ ; /doxs/ , /html/ to latest/api/ ). Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description python_version string 3.12 Python used to build the site. requirements string requirements-docs.txt Optional pip requirements file installed after the theme package (extra MkDocs plugins). Skipped when the file does not exist; the theme package already pins mkdocs, mkdocs-material, awesome-nav, pymdown and mike. theme_ref string empty Ref of hardfoc/hf-general-ci-tools to install the theme package from. Empty: the commit this workflow runs from, so the theme always matches the workflow. mkdocs_config string mkdocs.yml Path of mkdocs.yml. submodules string false Submodules to check out with the repository: 'false', 'true' (top level) or 'recursive'. submodule_paths string empty Space-separated submodule paths to initialise (shallow) after checkout, nested ones included: each parent submodule on the way is initialised without recursion, e.g. 'lib/core/drivers/internal/pincfg'. Use it instead of 'recursive' when the checks need a few nested submodules. check_commands string if [ -f tools/figkit/build.py ]; then python3 tools/figkit/build.py --check; fi if [ -f tools/docs/gen.py ]; then python3 tools/docs/gen.py --check; fi if [ ! -f tools/figkit/build.py ] && [ ! -f tools/docs/gen.py ]; then hardfoc-docs check; fi Shell lines run before the build, with GH_TOKEN set to the job's read-only token (for commands that read the GitHub API); any failure fails the job. The default runs the figure drift check and the generated-region check (hardfoc-docs check), or a repository's own tools/figkit and tools/docs/gen.py when it still carries them. doxygen_config string empty Doxyfile for the API reference, relative to doxygen_working_directory. docs.text: ru-yaml-lint ¶ Lint YAML files with yamllint against the repository's own rules. ru-yaml-lint.yml installs yamllint and runs it on every file matched by paths (comma-separated globs) that is not excluded by exclude_patterns , with config_file when it exists (yamllint's defaults otherwise).
